name: tenyr
why: A minimal 32-bit architecture with one instruction format and a simulated CPU, a strange and delightful environment to explore.

brief.what_it_is: tenyr is a 32-bit computer architecture and computing environment, described as focused on simplicity of design and implementation. It has three parts: an instruction set architecture, a Verilog hardware definition for FPGAs, and a set of software tools (assembler tas, linker tld, simulator tsim). Assembly source goes in, linked images come out, and tsim runs them on a simulated CPU. The README also ships a standard library of tenyr code and example programs such as Conway's Game of Life, a random snakes screensaver, and a recursive Fibonacci generator.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames tenyr as a simple 32-bit computer whose design and implementation are kept deliberately small. It does not state a broader motivation beyond that.
brief.how_it_works: The README gives no detailed mechanism. It names the pieces: an assembler (tas), a linker (tld), and a simulator (tsim), with the ISA documented in the project wiki. The Verilog hardware definition has been run on a Lattice ECP5 FPGA (ULX3S board) and a Xilinx Spartan6 FPGA (Nexys3 board), with VGA text output at 64x32.
brief.install_notes: The README gives no install steps and no commands. Running on real hardware requires an FPGA development board: the ULX3S (Lattice ECP5) or the Nexys3 (Xilinx Spartan6) have been demonstrated. The software tools are said to run on Mac, *nix, and Windows on multiple architectures. The homepage offers ZIP and TAR downloads, and the wiki holds the assembler, linker, and simulator docs.
brief.standout: The whole stack is small and self-contained: a custom ISA, a hand-rolled assembler, linker and simulator, and Verilog that runs on real FPGA boards, with example programs that have been shown running both in the simulator and on hardware. The homepage describes it as a simple environment, not a toy.
brief.status: Maintained as far as the pages show, but not confirmed. The GitHub page shows a C-language CI badge and a Codecov badge, and the project keeps a changelog from v0.9.4 onward. I did not find a release date or last-commit date in the fetched content, so recent activity is unverified.
brief.caveats: No input devices are implemented in hardware; the README asks for help with this. The hardware output is VGA text at 64x32 only. The FPGA demonstrations cover two specific boards. The README does not state a license. The scout note says the design has one instruction format, but the fetched README does not say that, so treat it as unverified. The Brew caveats field was empty.

judge.reason: A compact custom 32-bit architecture spanning assembler, linker, simulator, and FPGA hardware is a hands-on way to explore how computers work.

entry.title: tenyr
entry.tldr: A deliberately small 32-bit computer you can assemble, link and run in a simulator, with Verilog that also runs on real FPGA boards.
entry.deeper_look:
tenyr is a complete tiny computer, not just a program. It has three parts: an instruction set architecture, a Verilog hardware definition for FPGAs, and a set of software tools. The tools are an assembler (`tas`), a linker (`tld`) and a simulator (`tsim`). Assembly source goes through the assembler and linker, and the resulting image runs on the simulated CPU.

The README describes it as "a 32-bit computer architecture and computing environment that focuses on simplicity of design and implementation." It does not say more about why it was built. The project ships a standard library of tenyr code and example programs, including Conway's Game of Life, a random snakes screensaver and a recursive Fibonacci generator.

The idea underneath is that you can see the whole stack at once: the instruction set, the toolchain, the simulator and the hardware description. The same design has been demonstrated on a Lattice ECP5 FPGA (ULX3S board) and a Xilinx Spartan6 FPGA (Nexys3 board), with VGA text output at 64x32. The ISA is documented in the project wiki. If you have ever wondered what sits between assembly and gates, this is a small enough system to read through.
entry.install:
brew install tenyr
# installs tas, tld and tsim; depends on sdl2-compat and sdl2_image
# running on real hardware needs an FPGA board (ULX3S or Nexys3 have been demonstrated); the simulator needs none

try_this.what_happens: Shows the assembler's options, the first step from assembly source to an object file.
Shows the linker's options, which combine objects into a runnable image.
Shows the simulator's options. Run the example programs from the repository's ex/ directory with it, following the wiki.

entry.whats_unique: The whole stack is small and self-contained: a custom ISA, an assembler, linker and simulator, and Verilog that has run on real FPGA boards. The homepage calls it a simple environment, not a toy.
entry.caveats: No input devices are implemented in the hardware (the README asks for help), hardware output is VGA text at 64x32 only, and recent maintenance activity could not be confirmed.
